thread:
devon: FYI customer reported a sudden spike of 502s + TLS handshake failures when routing through their on-prem proxy to our hosted API after they flipped a NAT/proxy change earlier today. Repro steps below, can someone help triage?

devon: Repro (from their proxy):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/engines/list -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
*   Trying 18.214.12.34...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.com (18.214.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake error: Alert write:fatal:handshake_failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) OpenSSL SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.com:443 
```

devon: Their dig/nslookup shows the api hostname resolving to a public IP (18.214.12.34) instead of the VPC endpoint private IP (10.0.12.45). They said Private DNS was "on" when creating the interface endpoint but they're using an on-prem DNS forwarder -> VPC resolver chain.

ashley-p: Can you paste the dig +trace they ran and the resolver rule associations? My first guess is split-horizon / resolver rule not associated with the VPC/subnets that handle the endpoint.

devon: Here's the dig output they pasted: 
```
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; QUESTION SECTION:
;api.redwood.com.       IN A

;; ANSWER SECTION:
api.redwood.com. 300 IN CNAME proxy.customer.example.com.
proxy.customer.example.com. 60 IN A 18.214.12.34
```

mike-s: That CNAME to their proxy domain explains it — their conditional forwarder is returning an external A rather than resolving via the Route53 resolver into VPC. Two things to confirm: (1) the Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint exists and has rules to forward api.redwood.com -> VPC, (2) the VPC with the interface endpoint is associated with that resolver rule. If the resolver rule isn't associated with that VPC, the endpoint private DNS won't be used for on-prem queries.

devon: I also grabbed a tcpdump from their proxy (they shared sanitized output):
```
12:34:56.789 IP proxy->18.214.12.34: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
12:34:56.900 IP proxy->18.214.12.34: Flags [P.], seq 1:519, ack 1, win 229, length 518
12:34:57.001 TLS Client Hello SNI: api.redwood.com
12:34:57.150 RST from 18.214.12.34
```

mike-s: RSTs to the public IP make sense if the NLB/public cert isn't matching SNI / you're hitting a different frontend. If they were resolving to 10.0.12.45 they'd hit the interface endpoint and traffic would stay private.

support-bot: Suggested checklist: 
- Verify interface endpoint Private DNS is ENABLED for the service.
- Ensure Route53 Resolver inbound endpoint + rule exist and rule is ASSOCIATED with the customer's VPC(s).
- Confirm on-prem conditional forwarder points to the resolver inbound endpoint IPs (or use DNS firewall rules to force the zone).
- Check security groups on the interface endpoint allow the proxy's source CIDR.
See internal doc: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpce-dns (internal link)

sean: Quick mitigation if they need immediate fix: add a host override on their proxy for api.redwood.com -> 10.0.12.45 (not ideal long term). Example for linux proxy: 
```
echo "10.0.12.45 api.redwood.com" >> /etc/hosts && systemctl restart nscd || true
```

ashley-p: ^ only do host override for emergency. Strongly recommend fixing resolver associations instead. If you want to programmatically associate the rule: 
```
# associate resolver rule with VPC
aws route53resolver associate-resolver-rule --resolver-rule-id rslvr-rr-0abc123def --vpc-id vpc-0abcdef123 --region us-east-1
```

devon: Quick update: customer applied /etc/hosts workaround and now curl succeeds (200) from their proxy. They said the intermittent 401s also dropped after hitting the private endpoint — suspect NAT changed source IP earlier which triggered auth rate-limiting on their side.

mike-s: Yup — if proxy NAT changes source port/addr you can see auth token fences on the backend. For long term either preserve source IP (avoid double-NAT) or add X-Forwarded-For handling so auth checks can account for proxy. Also ensure SGs on the interface endpoint allow the proxy's egress IPs so no asymmetric path.

devon: I'll open a follow-up ticket with infra/networking to request resolver rule association + doc the steps and timeline for the customer. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ashley-p: Can you @infra-team and drop the resolver rule id + VPC id in that ticket? I'll add the rollback plan.

devon: Will do. Closing this thread for now — customer confirmed production is green with the hosts workaround.
